caption: What if every bit of oxygen gas vanished for just 5 seconds? Air is about 21% oxygen, so air pressure would suddenly drop to roughly what you feel 2 km up a mountain, and your ears would pop. Fire needs oxygen, so every diya, candle and gas stove would go out at once. Petrol and diesel engines burn their fuel with oxygen from the air, so every auto, bike and bus would stall. Rockets would not care: they carry their own oxygen, and ISRO's CE20 cryogenic engine burns liquid oxygen with liquid hydrogen. The real danger is breathing. Safety investigators warn that just one or two breaths of oxygen-free air can make a person faint, so the smart move is to hold your breath. Plot twist: only the gas vanished. Oxygen makes up about 65% of your body weight, mostly locked inside water. What would YOU miss first? 👇
